title: Copilot Studio: labelled and encrypted file uploads for agents on the Microsoft 365 channel
summary: Hold: the DLP automation omits the mandatory names for both the policy and the rule. The briefing also promises a change without settings changing and tells users that uploads depend on EXTRACT, although it correctly acknowledges elsewhere that the rollout default and upload-specific permission checks are not documented.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Scope: Existing file-input setting; Governance controls

claims.quote:
Go to the Settings page for your agent, and select Generative AI.
Navigate to the File processing capabilities section.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope: Existing file-input setting; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how planned labelled-file support interacts with File uploads.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "sensitivity" "uploads" "default"; "Copilot Studio" "sensitivity" "uploads" "switch". Opened image-input-analysis; it documents File uploads and says encrypted files are unsupported, without describing the planned interaction.

claims.claim: The Copilot DLP policy path is Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork.
claims.quote:
Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy.
Select the Custom template, then Custom policy.
On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.

claims.claim: The printed two-command PowerShell call creates the Copilot DLP policy and its blocking rule.
claims.quote:
New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences")
New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})
claims.fix: Both cmdlets require -Name, as confirmed in their parameter references. Replace the call with New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name <policy> -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @('CopilotExperiences'); New-DLPComplianceRule -Name <rule> -Policy <policy> -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting='ExcludeContentProcessing';value='Block'}). State that $loc and $advrule must first be defined using the cited reference's Copilot example.

claims.claim: The label-based rule uses Content contains > Sensitivity labels to exclude items from processing.
claims.quote: create DLP policies that use the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location with the Content contains > Sensitivity labels condition to exclude items from being processed.

claims.claim: Label encryption is configured in the Purview portal by creating or editing a label, then Access control > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now.
claims.quote:
When you select Configure access control settings on the Access control page to create or edit a sensitivity label, choose one of the following options:
Assign permissions now

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label> -EncryptionRightsDefinitions <rights> modifies label encryption rights.
claims.quote:
The EncryptionRightsDefinitions parameter specifies the rights users have when accessing protected.
This parameter is meaningful only when the EncryptionEnabled parameter value is either $true or $false and the EncryptionProtectionType parameter value is Template.
claims.fix: Qualify the existing-control note: this command edits admin-defined template encryption rights, not user-defined permissions; EncryptionRightsDefinitions is meaningful only with EncryptionProtectionType Template and an EncryptionEnabled value of $true or $false. Give the documented rights syntax Identity1:Rights1,Rights2;Identity2:Rights3,Rights4.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The existing file-input documentation says files encrypted through labels or password protection are unsupported.
claims.quote: Files with encryption, such as sensitivity labels or password protection, aren't supported.

claims.claim: For encrypted or password-protected Office uploads the agent tells users that it cannot read the file.
claims.quote: When a user uploads a password-protected or encrypted Office file, the agent tells the user that the file is encrypted or password-protected and can't be read.

claims.claim: Some rights-managed or label-encrypted uploads instead produce a generic error.
claims.quote: For some rights-managed or label-encrypted files, the agent returns a generic error instead.

claims.claim: The file-input article describes agents using the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: The standard harness is Copilot Studio's default agent runtime.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio standard harness default agent runtime. Opened harnesses-overview and read switch-experiences search excerpt; the sources describe multiple harnesses and a classic experience, not a product-wide default standard runtime.
claims.fix: Remove 'default' and use '(a Copilot Studio agent runtime)'; the cited file-input article establishes standard-harness scope without establishing which runtime is the product default.

claims.claim: The file-input page directs users to Microsoft Copilot Chat for sensitivity-labelled files.
claims.quote: use a Microsoft 365 experience such as Microsoft Copilot Chat, which supports sensitivity-labeled files.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels let users chat with an agent in Teams and Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: After you publish your agent at least once, you can connect it to the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels so users can chat with it in both Teams and Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: For documented Purview AI interactions, label-encrypted content requires EXTRACT as well as VIEW to return the data.
claims.quote: When the sensitivity label applies encryption, users must have the EXTRACT usage right, as well as VIEW, for the AI apps to return the data.

claims.claim: The Purview Copilot Studio page supports encryption only with sensitivity labels and only for the SharePoint knowledge source.
claims.quote: Encryption is supported only with sensitivity labels, and only for the SharePoint knowledge source.

claims.claim: The troubleshooting page instead says an agent cannot extract or ground on encrypted SharePoint content.
claims.quote: However, the agent can't extract or ground on content whose protection encrypts the file. This limitation includes sensitivity labels that apply encryption, Double Key Encryption (DKE), and password-protected files.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: General Copilot guidance ties the display of encrypted text to the user's effective EXTRACT right, which may differ from the label configuration.
claims.quote:
It's this usage right that determines whether Copilot or agents can display text to the user from encrypted content.
there are some situations that can result in the content's usage rights being different from the applied label configuration

claims.where: controls[3].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The person applying encryption is the Rights Management owner and always retains EXTRACT.
claims.quote: The person applying the encryption always has the EXTRACT usage right, because they are the Rights Management owner.

claims.claim: Full control (OWNER) includes EXTRACT.
claims.quote: Because the Full control (OWNER) usage right includes all the usage rights, EXTRACT is automatically included with Full control.

claims.claim: Purview displays EXTRACT as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, the EXTRACT usage right is displayed as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).

claims.claim: Copilot and agents have documented access restrictions for unopened SharePoint and OneDrive documents encrypted with user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents can't access unopened documents in SharePoint and OneDrive when they're labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions

claims.claim: Exceptions are a default label extending SharePoint permissions or direct reference by typing '/', both requiring EXTRACT.
claims.quote: unless the label is used as a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents or they're directly referenced by typing "/" (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Copilot DLP page says it does not scan files uploaded directly into Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts.
claims.quote: You can upload files when you craft a prompt for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Cowork to analyze. DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur.

claims.claim: Purview Data Security AI Admin is among the roles that can create or edit these Copilot DLP policies.
claims.quote:
Accounts with one of the following roles or role groups can create or edit a DLP policy
Purview Data Security AI Admin - Role for editing Data Loss Prevention policies related to Copilot and viewing AI content in Data Security Posture Management.

claims.claim: Administrators relying on the current block would lose it without any setting changing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "sensitivity" "uploads" "default"; "Copilot Studio" "sensitivity" "uploads" "switch". Opened image-input-analysis and roadmap; neither states the planned change takes effect without a setting change.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'If labelled-file support becomes available without an additional opt-in, administrators relying on the current block could lose it; Microsoft has not stated the rollout default.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The rollout checklist says upload results depend on each user's EXTRACT right while the risk section says upload-specific EXTRACT checks are undocumented.
claims.quote:
Microsoft has not documented whether uploads are checked for EXTRACT
Tell makers and users which labelled files agents may accept, once Microsoft documents it, and that results depend on each user's EXTRACT right.
claims.fix: Change the checklist item to: 'Tell makers and users which labelled files agents may accept and which effective permissions determine the result, once Microsoft documents the upload-specific checks.' Keep the general Copilot EXTRACT guidance explicitly separate from the planned upload feature.

claims.claim: The prepare rating treats the feature as arriving regardless of choice despite the page reporting an unknown default and no documented automatic change.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; defaultState: "unknown". Schema: a new capability whose default is not stated when no source says existing behaviour will change is review.
claims.fix: Set action to review on the evidence currently available. Reconsider prepare or act-now only when a source establishes an automatic change for existing agents or an administrator deadline.

claims.claim: Purview recommends enabling labels for SharePoint and OneDrive; otherwise accessible encrypted files are limited to data in use from Office apps on Windows.
claims.quote:
we recommend you enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive
When sensitivity labels aren't enabled for these services, the encrypted files that Copilot and agents can access are limited to data in use from Office apps on Windows.
